existing_requirement_decisions.new_text: When the triggering conditions of paragraph 5.1.2. are achieved, the ACPE shall limit vehicle acceleration in order to prevent or mitigate a collision with an obstacle located not more than 1.5 m in front of or behind the vehicle, in the vehicle path, provided the conditions in paragraph 5.1.5. (a) to (d) are met. These include: road flat, horizontal and dry; weather not affecting performance; tyres, brakes, load, powertrain in proper state; no trailer; rear hatches, trunk lids or tailgates closed and latched; no sensing impairment (at least 1000 Lux, non-extreme target RCS/shape, no significant weather, no overhead obstructions); a stationary, unobstructed obstacle clearly separated from other objects; lateral alignment by obstacle type (vehicle centre line between the vehicle's outer-edge planes, wall overlap at least 1.0 m, pedestrian centre line within 25 per cent of vehicle width); straight travel in lane; obstacle an M1 vehicle, wall-like structure (at least 2.0 m wide, 1.0 m high) or pedestrian silhouette; obstacle at least 1.0 m away at the trigger; vehicle at or below maximum creeping speed forward and at or below 4 km/h rearward.
existing_requirement_decisions.reason: The obstacle range changed from 1.0-1.5 m to not more than 1.5 m. The trigger is now the 5.1.2 triggering conditions rather than accelerator application. A closed/latched rear hatch condition was added. The 0.2 m lateral offset was replaced by obstacle-type-specific criteria. Pedestrian obstacles were added. A speed condition (creeping speed forward, 4 km/h rearward) was added. These change the conditions of the obligation.

existing_requirement_decisions.new_text: For the accelerator control misapplication test, the lateral offset between the centreline of the vehicle target and the centreline of the vehicle shall be between 0.0 m and the distance to the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
existing_requirement_decisions.reason: The old limit of 0.0 m to 0.2 m is replaced in new 6.5.2 by 0.0 m to the distance to the extreme outer edge of the vehicle. This is a substantive change to the offset range. The new text also names the 'vehicle target'. New 6.5.3 sets a separate limit for a pedestrian obstacle, and that belongs in Track B.

existing_requirement_decisions.new_text: The test procedures shall be performed both in a forward and rearward direction and at least with the ACPE interventions triggered at 1.0 m (+0.1 m tolerance) and 1.5 m (-0.1 m tolerance) distance from the target position (as detailed in Table 1).
existing_requirement_decisions.reason: New 6.6 drops the requirement to perform the test with and without an expected ACPE intervention. It also changes the reference point from the vehicle's position at the start of the test to the distance from the target at which the ACPE interventions are triggered. The forward/rearward directions and the 1.0 m and 1.5 m distances with their tolerances are retained.

Old Table 1 step (a) is carried into new 6.6.1.2(a) for stationary vehicles. The only word edit is the insertion of 'relevant' before 'target', which clarifies which target applies and does not change the obligation. Table 1 still defines the distances. The creeping-vehicle procedure in 6.6.2 is a new separate situation and does not alter this obligation.

New 6.6.1.2(b) is word-for-word identical to old step (b): hold the vehicle stationary and select the corresponding driving direction. The creeping procedure 6.6.2.2(b) repeats it, so the obligation is retained.

New 6.6.1.2(c) is identical to old step (c): accelerate with steering neutral, achieve the triggering conditions of 5.1.2 before the vehicle reaches 0.5 km/h. The referenced 5.1.2 gained 'resulting in continuous acceleration', but that edit belongs to 5.1.2 and is not a change to this test step. The creeping variant in 6.6.2.2(d) is a separate new procedure.
New 6.6.1.2(d) is identical to old step (d): record the speed at the collision point (if applicable) or at the respective speed measurement point. There are no word changes.

The old sentence allowed, at the manufacturer's request, driving up to 20 m to the start position and/or switching the engine off and on before a test. The new 6.6.1.2 and 6.6.2.2 and the new Table 1 contain no such provision. The candidate clauses (6.4.2, 5.2.3.1.1, 5.4.2) cover unrelated subjects. The permission is therefore dropped.

obligations.text: This UN Regulation applies to the type approval of vehicles of Category M1 and N1 equipped with automatic transmission with regard to their Acceleration Control for Pedal Error systems (ACPE).

obligations.text: Vehicles where installation of means of forward and/or rear detection is incompatible with their intended use may be exempted from the relevant requirements (forward and/or rear direction) of this Regulation, subject to the decision of the Type Approval Authority.
obligations.reason: Same exemption as old 1.3; the condition wording changed from 'on-road use' to 'intended use', broadening the applicability condition.

coverage.source_unit: 1.4 – permission: completed vehicles built on a base vehicle lacking the structure for forward/rear detection means may be exempted from the relevant requirements, subject to Type Approval Authority decision

obligations.text: Completed vehicles built on a base vehicle which did not have the necessary structure to allow installation of means of forward and/or rear detection may be exempted from the relevant requirements (forward and/or rear direction) of this Regulation, subject to the decision of the Type Approval Authority.
obligations.reason: Paragraph 1.4 is new. Candidate o005 (1.3) covers a different applicability case (vehicles where installation is incompatible with on-road use), whereas this covers completed vehicles built on a base vehicle lacking the necessary structure. No positive evidence that it replaces o005, so it is a separate scoped exemption.

coverage.exclusion_reason: Definition only; creates no independent obligation.

coverage.source_unit: 2.3 – definition of common space
2.4 (a)-(b) – definition of dry road affording good adhesion
2.5 intro: definition of sufficient nominal PBC
coverage.exclusion_reason: Definition lead-in; the value criteria are mapped in the items below.

coverage.source_unit: 2.5(a) 0.9 with ASTM E1136-19 tyre per E1337-19 at 40 mph
2.5(b)(i)-(ii) 1.017 with ASTM F2493-20 tyre or k-test per R13-H
2.5(c) required value for design max deceleration, k-test per R13 Annex 13

obligations.text: A road surface has a sufficient nominal Peak Braking Coefficient (PBC) if its friction coefficient is 0.9 when measured using the ASTM E1136-19 standard reference test tyre in accordance with ASTM Method E1337-19 at a speed of 40 mph.
obligations.reason: Same scoped definition criterion as old 2.5(a) (o011), same paragraph number; only a typographical wording change.

obligations.text: A road surface has a sufficient nominal PBC if its friction coefficient is 1.017 when measured using either (i) the ASTM F2493-20 standard reference test tyre in accordance with ASTM Method E1337-19 at 40 mph, or (ii) the k-test method in Appendix 2 to Annex 6 of UN Regulation No. 13-H.
obligations.reason: Identical criterion as old 2.5(b) (o011).

obligations.text: A road surface has a sufficient nominal PBC if its friction coefficient has the value required to permit the design maximum deceleration of the relevant vehicle, when measured using the k-test method in Appendix 2 to Annex 13 of UN Regulation No. 13.
obligations.reason: Identical criterion as old 2.5(c) (o011).

coverage.source_unit: 2.6 definition of Self-check

obligations.text: "Self-check" means an integrated function that checks for a system failure on a continuous basis at least while the system is active.
obligations.reason: Unchanged definition identical to old 2.6 (o012).

coverage.source_unit: 2.7 definition of Obstacle

obligations.text: "Obstacle" means either a vehicle, a wall-like structure or a pedestrian.
obligations.reason: Replaces old 2.7 (o013), which defined Obstacle as a vehicle or wall-like structure; a pedestrian has been added.

coverage.source_unit: 2.8 definition of Automatic Transmission

obligations.text: "Automatic Transmission" means any transmission which does not require the use of a clutch control by the driver in order to shift gears (including single gear transmissions, continuously-variable transmissions, transmissions with an automated clutch).
obligations.reason: Unchanged definition identical to old 2.8 (o014).

coverage.source_unit: 2.9 definition of Mass of a vehicle in running order

obligations.text: "Mass of a vehicle in running order" means the mass of an unladen vehicle with bodywork, including coolant, oils, at least 90 per cent of fuel, 100 per cent of other liquids, driver (75 kg), but excluding used waters, tools, spare wheel.
obligations.reason: Unchanged definition identical to old 2.9 (o015).

coverage.source_unit: 2.10 definition of Extreme outer edge, with exclusions (a)-(d)

obligations.text: "Extreme outer edge" on either side of the vehicle means the plane parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle and touching its lateral outer edge, disregarding the projection of: (a) tyres near their ground contact point and tyre-pressure gauge connections; (b) anti-skid devices mounted on the wheels; (c) devices for indirect vision; (d) side direction-indicator lamps, end-outline marker lamps, front and rear position lamps, parking lamps, retro-reflectors and side-marker lamps.
obligations.reason: New definition with no equivalent among candidates; o011, o163 and o147 are unrelated in scope, and paragraph 2.10 is not a renumbering of any of them.

coverage.source_unit: 2.11 definition of "Vehicle width" as distance between the two vertical planes defined in 2.10
coverage.exclusion_reason: Definition only; imposes no engineering, test or compliance obligation by itself.

coverage.source_unit: 2.12 definition of "Moving off"
2.13 definition of "Maximum Creeping Speed"
2.13.1 definition of "Creeping"
2.14 definition of "Reducing the effective demand of the accelerator control to zero" including exclusion of non-pedal-related torque demand
3. heading "Application for approval"
3.1 – application for approval shall be submitted by manufacturer or authorized representative

obligations.text: The application for approval of a vehicle type with regard to the ACPE shall be submitted by the vehicle manufacturer or by his authorized representative.
obligations.reason: Identical wording, same actor, action and scope as old clause o017 under the same parent 'Application for approval'; same paragraph number.

coverage.source_unit: 3.2 – application shall be accompanied by documents in triplicate (list introduced)

obligations.text: The application for approval shall be accompanied by the documents mentioned below, submitted in triplicate.
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation as old clause o018 (3.2) under the same parent; identical wording and applicability.

coverage.source_unit: 3.3 first sentence – description of vehicle type per para 2.2 plus documentation package giving access to basic ACPE design and its links/control of output variables
3.3 second sentence – numbers/symbols identifying the vehicle type shall be specified

obligations.text: The application shall include a description of the vehicle type with regard to the items in paragraph 2.2, together with a documentation package giving access to the basic design of the ACPE and the means by which it is linked to other vehicle systems or by which it directly controls output variables.
obligations.reason: Same documentation requirement as old clause o019 (3.3), same parent and scope; wording unchanged.

obligations.text: The numbers and/or symbols identifying the vehicle type shall be specified in the application documentation.
obligations.reason: Same sentence within old clause o019 (3.3); unchanged scope and actor.

coverage.source_unit: 3.4 – representative vehicle shall be submitted to Technical Service conducting approval tests

obligations.text: A vehicle representative of the vehicle type to be approved shall be submitted to the Technical Service conducting the approval tests.
obligations.reason: Identical to old clause o020 (3.4) with the same parent, actor and scope.

coverage.source_unit: 4 – heading 'Approval'
4.1 – approval shall be granted if vehicle type meets requirements of paragraph 5

obligations.text: If the vehicle type submitted for approval pursuant to this Regulation meets the requirements of paragraph 5, approval of that vehicle type shall be granted.
obligations.reason: Identical to old clause o022 (4.1) under the same 'Approval' parent; same condition and action.

coverage.source_unit: 4.2 first clause: approval number shall be assigned to each approved vehicle type, first two digits indicating amendment series (00 initial form)
4.2 second sentence: same Contracting Party shall not assign same number to same vehicle type with another ACPE type or to another vehicle type

obligations.text: An approval number shall be assigned to each vehicle type approved; its first two digits (00 for the Regulation in its initial form) shall indicate the series of amendments incorporating the most recent major technical amendments at the time of issue of the approval.
obligations.reason: Identical to old 4.2 (o023) under the same Approval parent; same actor, action and scope.

obligations.text: The same Contracting Party shall not assign the same approval number to the same vehicle type equipped with another type of ACPE, or to another vehicle type.
obligations.reason: Identical prohibition in old 4.2 (o023); same scope and continuity.

coverage.source_unit: 4.3 notice of approval, refusal or withdrawal communicated to Parties using Annex 1 form with photographs/plans (max A4, appropriate scale)

obligations.text: Notice of approval, refusal or withdrawal of approval shall be communicated to the Parties to the Agreement applying this Regulation by means of a form conforming to the model in Annex 1 and photographs and/or plans supplied by the applicant, in a format not exceeding A4 (210 x 297 mm) or folded to that format, and on an appropriate scale.
obligations.reason: Identical to old 4.3 (o024); same communication obligation and scope.

coverage.source_unit: 4.4 intro: approval mark affixed conspicuously in readily accessible place specified on approval form to every conforming vehicle, per Annex 2

obligations.text: An international approval mark conforming to the model described in Annex 2 shall be affixed, conspicuously and in a readily accessible place specified on the approval form, to every vehicle conforming to a vehicle type approved under this Regulation.
obligations.reason: Identical to old 4.4 (o025); same marking obligation.

coverage.source_unit: 4.4.1 approval mark element: circle surrounding letter E followed by distinguishing number of approving country
Footnote 2 on distinguishing numbers reference
coverage.exclusion_reason: Informational reference footnote, not an obligation.

obligations.text: The approval mark shall include a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
obligations.reason: Identical to old 4.4.1 (o026) under the same 4.4 marking parent.

coverage.source_unit: 4.4.2 approval mark element: Regulation number, letter R, dash, approval number to right of circle

obligations.text: The approval mark shall include the number of this Regulation, followed by the letter "R", a dash and the approval number, placed to the right of the circle prescribed in paragraph 4.4.1.
obligations.reason: Identical to old 4.4.2 (o027); same marking element and scope.

coverage.source_unit: 4.5 permission: symbol of 4.4.1 need not be repeated if vehicle also approved under other Regulations in same country
4.5 'in such a case' requirement: Regulation and approval numbers and additional symbols placed in vertical columns right of 4.4.1 symbol

obligations.text: If the vehicle conforms to a vehicle type approved under one or more other Regulations annexed to the Agreement in the country which has granted approval under this Regulation, the symbol prescribed in paragraph 4.4.1 need not be repeated.
obligations.reason: Identical permission in old 4.5 (o028); same applicability.

obligations.text: Where the symbol of paragraph 4.4.1 is not repeated for a vehicle approved under other Regulations in the same country, the Regulation and approval numbers and the additional symbols shall be placed in vertical columns to the right of the symbol prescribed in paragraph 4.4.1.
obligations.reason: Identical placement requirement in old 4.5 (o028); same condition and scope.

coverage.source_unit: 4.6 approval mark shall be clearly legible and indelible (single requirement)

obligations.text: The approval mark shall be clearly legible and be indelible.
obligations.reason: Identical wording, same paragraph number 4.6 and same parent 'Approval'; matches old clause o029 in actor, object and scope.

coverage.source_unit: 4.7 approval mark placement close to or on vehicle data plate

obligations.text: The approval mark shall be placed close to or on the vehicle data plate.
obligations.reason: Same paragraph 4.7 under Approval; identical scope to old clause o030.

coverage.source_unit: 5. Specifications heading
5.1 applicability condition: performance requirements apply to vehicle with no trailer, mass between maximum mass and mass in running order, powertrain management system properly operational

obligations.text: The performance requirements of paragraph 5.1 shall apply to a vehicle with no trailer coupled, with a mass between maximum mass and mass in running order, and whose powertrain management system is properly operational.
obligations.reason: Identical to old clause o032 (5.1) under the same parent Specifications; same applicability scope.

coverage.source_unit: 5.1.1(a) obstacle in front, driving direction forward
5.1.1(b) obstacle behind, driving direction rearwards

obligations.text: The ACPE shall be able to limit unintended acceleration of the vehicle when an accelerator control misapplication by the driver has been detected, at least when an obstacle exists in front of the vehicle and the driving direction is selected to be forward.
obligations.reason: Same paragraph 5.1.1 with identical wording as old o033 item (a); same case and scope.

obligations.text: The ACPE shall be able to limit unintended acceleration of the vehicle when an accelerator control misapplication by the driver has been detected, at least when an obstacle exists behind the vehicle and the driving direction is selected to be rearwards.
obligations.reason: Same paragraph 5.1.1 with identical wording as old o033 item (b); same case and scope.

coverage.source_unit: 5.1.2 definition of accelerator control misapplication (continuous acceleration, velocity >=400%/s over >=70% travel, reaching >=90% position)

obligations.text: An accelerator control application resulting in continuous acceleration and having a velocity of at least 400 per cent per second over a travel distance of at least 70 per cent of the total travel distance of the accelerator control, and reaching a maximum position of at least 90 per cent with that velocity, shall be regarded as an accelerator control misapplication in the context of paragraph 5.1.1.
obligations.reason: Replaces old o034 (same paragraph 5.1.2, same criterion) with the added condition 'resulting in continuous acceleration', which changes the scope of the misapplication definition.

coverage.source_unit: 5.1.3 first sentence: in force-based ACPE triggering systems, force above the threshold is considered misapplication
5.1.3 second sentence: manufacturer justifies threshold to Type Approval Authority

obligations.text: For ACPE systems that implement force-based triggering, notwithstanding paragraph 5.1.2, an accelerator control force greater than the triggering threshold shall be considered accelerator control misapplication.
obligations.reason: Same scoped requirement as old 5.1.3 (o035), identical wording and parent context, no substantive change.

obligations.text: For ACPE systems that implement force-based triggering, the manufacturer shall justify the triggering threshold to the satisfaction of the Type Approval Authority.
obligations.reason: Same manufacturer justification duty as old 5.1.3 (o035), unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 5.1.4: ACPE controls acceleration when accelerated from standstill
5.1.4: ACPE controls acceleration, as relevant, while creeping

obligations.text: The ACPE shall control acceleration when the vehicle is accelerated from standstill.
obligations.reason: Same requirement as old 5.1.4 (o036), same paragraph number, unchanged for the standstill case.

obligations.text: The ACPE shall control acceleration, as relevant, when the vehicle is accelerated while creeping.
obligations.reason: The creeping case was not in old 5.1.4 (o036), which covered standstill only. It is a separately applicable operating case.

coverage.source_unit: 5.1.4.1(a): no ACPE intervention required when an AEBS warning or intervention is occurring
5.1.4.1(b): no ACPE intervention required when vehicle speed is greater than 10 km/h

obligations.text: An ACPE intervention is not required when there is an AEBS warning or intervention occurring.
obligations.reason: New exemption. Old 5.1.4.1 (o037) concerned the ACPE readiness indication, not an intervention exemption. Old 5.3.2 (o062) concerned failure warning suppression.

obligations.text: An ACPE intervention is not required when the vehicle speed is greater than 10 km/h.
obligations.reason: New exemption from intervention above 10 km/h. The old 10 km/h wording (o062) applied to failure-warning suppression, which is a different scope.

coverage.source_unit: 5.1.4.2 whole clause: indicate ACPE-not-ready status to driver 6 s after powertrain initiation, until successfully initialised

obligations.text: If the ACPE is not ready to perform an intervention 6 s after the initiation of the vehicle powertrain, information of this status shall be indicated to the driver, and this information shall persist until the system has been successfully initialised.
obligations.reason: Renumbering of old 5.1.4.1 (o037). Same actor, 6 s condition, driver indication and persistence until initialisation; only 'seconds' became 's'. The new 5.1.4.1 is a different, new exemption.

coverage.source_unit: 5.1.5 main clause: ACPE limits acceleration for obstacle not more than 1.5 m ahead/behind at triggering
5.1.5(a)(i)-(ii): road and weather conditions
5.1.5(b)(i)-(v): tyres, brakes, load distribution, no trailer/mass, powertrain
5.1.5(b)(vi): rear hatches, trunk lids, tailgates closed and latched
5.1.5(c)(i)-(iv): sensing-capability conditions
5.1.5(d)(i): obstacle stationary, unobstructed, separated
5.1.5(d)(ii): vehicle obstacle centre line within vehicle outer planes
5.1.5(d)(iii): wall obstacle overlap at least 1.0 m
5.1.5(d)(iv): pedestrian obstacle offset not more than 25 per cent of vehicle width
5.1.5(d)(v): straight direction of travel
5.1.5(d)(vi): obstacle type and size
5.1.5(d)(vii): obstacle at least 1.0 m at triggering
5.1.5(d)(viii): speed at or below max creeping speed forward and 4 km/h rearward
Footnote 3: condition to be reviewed by September 2032
coverage.exclusion_reason: Review/administrative note about a future review of the (d)(viii) condition; it creates no engineering or product requirement.

obligations.text: The ACPE shall limit vehicle acceleration in order to prevent or mitigate a collision with an obstacle located not more than 1.5 m in front of or behind the vehicle, in the vehicle path, at the time the triggering conditions (paragraph 5.1.2) are achieved, provided the conditions of paragraph 5.1.5(a) to (d) are met.
obligations.reason: Replaces old 5.1.5 (o038) core requirement. The distance range changed from 1.0-1.5 m to not more than 1.5 m, and the timing changed from 'accelerator control is applied' to 'triggering conditions of 5.1.2 are achieved'.

obligations.text: The ACPE shall limit acceleration for an obstacle not more than 1.5 m in front of or behind the vehicle, provided external influences allow it: the road is flat, horizontal and dry affording good adhesion, and weather conditions do not affect vehicle performance (e.g. no storm, not below 0°C).
obligations.reason: Same condition as old 5.1.5(a)(i)-(ii) (o038), unchanged.

obligations.text: The ACPE shall limit acceleration for an obstacle not more than 1.5 m in front of or behind the vehicle, provided the vehicle state allows it: tyres in appropriate state and properly inflated; brakes, if intended to be used, properly operational; no severe uneven load distribution; no trailer coupled and mass between maximum mass and mass in running order; powertrain management system properly operational.
obligations.reason: Same conditions as old 5.1.5(b)(i)-(v) (o038), unchanged.

obligations.text: The ACPE shall limit acceleration for an obstacle not more than 1.5 m in front of or behind the vehicle, provided that, if the vehicle is equipped with rear hatches, trunk lids or tailgates, they are closed and latched in the normal conditions of vehicle operation.
obligations.reason: Condition (b)(vi) is absent from old 5.1.5(b) (o038), which ends at (b)(v).

obligations.text: The ACPE shall limit acceleration for an obstacle not more than 1.5 m in front of or behind the vehicle, provided there are no external influences affecting sensing: ambient illumination at least 1000 Lux and no extreme sensor blinding; target vehicle not extreme in RCS or silhouette (e.g. below fifth percentile of RCS of all M1 vehicles); no significant weather affecting sensing (heavy rain, dense fog, snow, dirt); no overhead obstructions close to the vehicle.
obligations.reason: Same conditions as old 5.1.5(c)(i)-(iv) (o038), unchanged.

obligations.text: The ACPE shall limit acceleration for an obstacle not more than 1.5 m in front of or behind the vehicle, provided the obstacle is stationary, unobstructed and clearly separated from other objects in the driving direction.
obligations.reason: Same as old 5.1.5(d)(i) (o038), unchanged.

obligations.text: The ACPE shall limit acceleration for an obstacle not more than 1.5 m in front of or behind the vehicle, provided that, for a vehicle obstacle, the centre line of the obstacle lies between two vertical longitudinal planes defining the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
obligations.reason: Replaces old 5.1.5(d)(ii) (o038), a lateral offset of at most 0.2 m between centrelines, with a centre-line-within-vehicle-width criterion for vehicle obstacles.

obligations.text: The ACPE shall limit acceleration for an obstacle not more than 1.5 m in front of or behind the vehicle, provided that, for a wall obstacle, the overlap between wall and vehicle is at least 1.0 m.
obligations.reason: The wall overlap criterion has no counterpart in old 5.1.5 (o038).

obligations.text: The ACPE shall limit acceleration for an obstacle not more than 1.5 m in front of or behind the vehicle, provided that, for a pedestrian obstacle, the distance between the centre line of the pedestrian obstacle and the centre line of the vehicle is not more than 25 per cent of the vehicle width.
obligations.reason: The pedestrian obstacle case is new and absent from old 5.1.5 (o038).

obligations.text: The ACPE shall limit acceleration for an obstacle not more than 1.5 m in front of or behind the vehicle, provided the direction of travel is straight with no curve, and the vehicle is not turning at an intersection and is following its lane.
obligations.reason: Same as old 5.1.5(d)(iii) (o038), renumbered within the list.

obligations.text: The ACPE shall limit acceleration for an obstacle not more than 1.5 m in front of or behind the vehicle, provided the obstacle is a vehicle of category M1, or a wall-like structure at least 2.0 m wide and at least 1.0 m high, or a silhouette of a pedestrian that relates to a human being.
obligations.reason: Replaces old 5.1.5(d)(iv) (o038) obstacle types; the pedestrian silhouette is added.

obligations.text: The ACPE shall limit acceleration for an obstacle not more than 1.5 m in front of or behind the vehicle, provided the obstacle is located at least 1.0 m from the vehicle at the time the triggering conditions (paragraph 5.1.2) are achieved.
obligations.reason: Replaces the lower bound of the old 5.1.5 (o038) 'between 1.0 m and 1.5 m' range with a separate condition tied to the triggering conditions.

obligations.text: The ACPE shall limit acceleration for an obstacle not more than 1.5 m in front of or behind the vehicle, provided the vehicle is travelling at or below its maximum creeping speed in the forward direction and at or below 4 km/h in the rearward direction.
obligations.reason: The speed condition is not present in old 5.1.5 (o038).

coverage.source_unit: 5.1.5.1 sentence 1: system shall not deactivate or unreasonably switch control strategy when conditions deviate
5.1.5.1 sentence 2: manufacturer demonstrates per Annex 3
5.1.5.1 sentence 2 permission: Technical Service may test under deviating conditions if justified
5.1.5.1 sentence 3: rationale and results appended to test report

obligations.text: When conditions deviate from those listed in paragraph 5.1.5, the system shall not deactivate or unreasonably switch the control strategy.
obligations.reason: Relocated from the closing paragraph of old 5.1.5 (o038) into its own paragraph. Same actor, action and scope.

obligations.text: The manufacturer shall demonstrate, in accordance with Annex 3 of this Regulation, that the system does not deactivate or unreasonably switch the control strategy when conditions deviate from those listed in paragraph 5.1.5.
obligations.reason: Relocated from the closing paragraph of old 5.1.5 (o038). Same manufacturer demonstration per Annex 3.

obligations.text: If deemed justified, the manufacturer's Annex 3 demonstration may be followed by testing by the Technical Service in conditions deviating from those listed in paragraph 5.1.5 or those in paragraph 6.
obligations.reason: Relocated permission from the closing paragraph of old 5.1.5 (o038), unchanged.

obligations.text: The rationale for and the results of the verification testing under deviating conditions shall be appended to the test report.
obligations.reason: Relocated reporting duty from the closing paragraph of old 5.1.5 (o038), unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 5.1.6. ACPE performance (heading only)
coverage.exclusion_reason: Heading only; no obligation text. Requirement now sits in 5.1.6.1.

coverage.source_unit: 5.1.6.1 first sentence: collision speed no greater than 8 km/h above speed at triggering conditions of 5.1.2
5.1.6.1 second sentence: collision speed not greater than 70 per cent of speed without ACPE intervention

obligations.text: In the case that a collision is not prevented (acceleration from standstill), the collision speed shall be no greater than 8 km/h higher than the vehicle speed at the point where the triggering conditions specified in paragraph 5.1.2 are met.
obligations.reason: Same collision-speed limit as old 5.1.6 (first sentence), relocated to subparagraph 5.1.6.1 with a heading; same actor, condition and value.

obligations.text: In the case that a collision is not prevented (acceleration from standstill), the collision speed shall not be greater than 70 per cent of the speed the vehicle would have had in the same position and under the same circumstances without any ACPE intervention.
obligations.reason: Same 70% limit as old 5.1.6 (second sentence), relocated to 5.1.6.1; '%' changed to 'per cent' only.

coverage.source_unit: 5.1.6.1.1 low power to weight vehicles: at least 15 per cent speed reduction where 30 per cent cannot be achieved

obligations.text: For vehicles that do not exceed 8 km/h without ACPE in the test scenarios but for which a speed reduction of 30 per cent cannot be achieved due to a low engine power to test mass ratio, the speed reduction shall be at least 15 per cent.
obligations.reason: Old 5.1.6.1 carried the same low power-to-mass relaxation (8 km/h, 30%→15%) under old 5.1.6; it is renumbered to 5.1.6.1.1 with the same scope and values.

coverage.source_unit: 5.1.6.2 acceleration while creeping: ACPE reduces effective accelerator demand to zero at or before collision

obligations.text: For the acceleration-while-creeping case, if a collision is not prevented, the ACPE shall reduce the effective demand of the accelerator control to zero at or before the point of collision.
obligations.reason: No candidate has this requirement; old 5.1.11.2 concerns driver interruption and 5.1.6 concerns collision speed limits. The creeping-case demand-to-zero requirement is a separate obligation.

coverage.source_unit: 5.1.7 sentence 1: acceleration continues to be limited by ACPE during any intervention
5.1.7 sentence 2: intervention may be ended when obstacle no longer detected or driver interrupted (permission)
5.1.7 sentence 3: manufacturer declares ACPE continuation conditions to technical service

obligations.text: During any intervention, the vehicle acceleration shall continue to be limited by the ACPE.
obligations.reason: Identical to old 5.1.7 with the same paragraph number and scope.

obligations.text: The ACPE intervention may be ended when the obstacle is no longer detected, or the driver has interrupted the function.
obligations.reason: Identical permission in old 5.1.7, same paragraph and scope.

obligations.text: The manufacturer shall declare the ACPE continuation conditions to the technical service.
obligations.reason: Identical manufacturer obligation in old 5.1.7, same paragraph and scope.

coverage.source_unit: 5.1.8 sentence 1: ACPE effectiveness not adversely affected by magnetic or electrical fields
5.1.8 sentence 2: demonstrate by fulfilling UN R10 06 or later series requirements and transitional provisions

obligations.text: The effectiveness of ACPE shall not be adversely affected by magnetic or electrical fields.
obligations.reason: Identical to old 5.1.8, same paragraph and scope.

obligations.text: Non-susceptibility to magnetic or electrical fields shall be demonstrated by fulfilling the technical requirements and respecting the transitional provisions of the 06 or later series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 10.
obligations.reason: Identical demonstration requirement in old 5.1.8, same paragraph and scope.

coverage.source_unit: 5.1.9 whole sentence: conformity with safety aspects of electronic control systems shown by meeting Annex 3

obligations.text: Conformity with the safety aspects of electronic control systems shall be shown by meeting the requirements of Annex 3 (applies to a vehicle with no trailer coupled, mass between maximum mass and mass in running order, powertrain management system properly operational).
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation as old 5.1.9 (o043), identical wording, same parent 5.1 context; paragraph number unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 5.1.10 whole sentence: ACPE informs driver of intervention per 5.4.2

obligations.text: The ACPE shall inform the driver of its intervention in accordance with paragraph 5.4.2.
obligations.reason: Same actor, action and scope as old 5.1.10 (o044) under the same parent 5.1; unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 5.1.11 heading: Interruption of ACPE by driver
5.1.11.1 first sentence: ACPE shall provide a means for driver to interrupt its intervention
5.1.11.1 second sentence: interruption started by any intentional action indicating driver has recognised the situation

obligations.text: The ACPE shall provide a means for the driver to interrupt its intervention.
obligations.reason: Same obligation as old 5.1.11.1 (o046), same parent 5.1.11; unchanged.

obligations.text: The driver's interruption of the ACPE intervention shall be started by any intentional action which indicates that the driver has recognised the situation.
obligations.reason: Same sentence within old 5.1.11.1 (o046); unchanged design constraint on the interruption trigger.

coverage.source_unit: 5.1.11.2 whole sentence: interruption by maintaining accelerator control application, no rapid increase of acceleration

obligations.text: In the case of interruption of the ACPE by maintaining the accelerator control application, there shall be no rapid increase of acceleration.
obligations.reason: Identical to old 5.1.11.2 (o047), same parent 5.1.11 and scope.

coverage.source_unit: 5.1.11.3 whole sentence: manufacturer documents and demonstrates fulfilment to Approval Authority during safety concept inspection per Annex 3

obligations.text: The manufacturer shall document and demonstrate fulfilment of the ACPE driver-interruption requirements (5.1.11) to the Approval Authority during the inspection of the safety concept as part of the assessment to Annex 3.
obligations.reason: Same obligation as old 5.1.11.3 (o048), same parent 5.1.11 and same scope; unchanged wording.

coverage.source_unit: 5.1.12 whole sentence: performance requirements verified using test procedure in sections 6.6.1 and 6.6.2

obligations.text: The performance requirements of paragraph 5.1 (vehicle with no trailer coupled, mass between maximum mass and mass in running order, powertrain management system properly operational) shall be verified using the test procedure described in sections 6.6.1. and 6.6.2.
obligations.reason: Same scoped verification obligation as old o049 (5.1.12, same paragraph number, same actor/object); the referenced test procedure changed from section 6 to sections 6.6.1 and 6.6.2.

coverage.source_unit: 5.2 heading 'Deactivation'
5.2.1 sentence 1: ACPE automatically reinstated at each new engine start when manual deactivation means is fitted
5.2.1 sentence 2: exception for automatically performed engine starts (e.g. stop/start)
5.2.1 sentence 3: deactivation warning at least at time of deactivation

obligations.text: When a vehicle is equipped with a means to manually deactivate the ACPE, the ACPE shall be automatically reinstated at the initiation of any new engine start (or run cycle, as relevant).
obligations.reason: Identical to old o051 5.2.1 sentence 1: same actor, condition and action.

obligations.text: The requirement for automatic reinstatement of the ACPE at a new engine start (or run cycle) does not apply when the new engine start (or run cycle, as relevant) is performed automatically, e.g., the operation of a stop/start system.
obligations.reason: Same exception as old o051 5.2.1 sentence 2, same scope.

obligations.text: For a vehicle equipped with a means to manually deactivate the ACPE, a deactivation warning shall be given at least at the time of deactivation.
obligations.reason: Same warning requirement as old o051 5.2.1 sentence 3.

coverage.source_unit: 5.2.2 permission: long term deactivation means, no reinstatement at each engine start
5.2.2 driver information by (a), (b) or (c) with sub-options
5.2.2 last sentence: not possible with less than two deliberate actions

obligations.text: Notwithstanding paragraph 5.2.1., a vehicle may be equipped with a long term deactivation means to manually deactivate the ACPE; in that case the system is not required to be reinstated at the initiation of each engine start (or run cycle, as relevant).
obligations.reason: Same permission as old o052 5.2.2, unchanged.

obligations.text: A vehicle with long term deactivation shall provide information to the driver by either (a), (b) or (c): (a) a constant optical warning signal informing that the ACPE is deactivated (the yellow warning signal of 5.4.3. may be used); (b) periodic driver information that the ACPE is deactivated, given for a minimum of 10 seconds or until driver confirmation, at least every 7 days or every 10 engine starts (or run cycles), not counting automatic engine starts such as stop/start, and distinct from the failure warning signal of 5.4.3.; or (c) if deactivation is only for one direction (forward or rearwards), as an alternative to (a) or (b), a constant optical warning when that driving direction is first selected after each initiation of the powertrain, remaining at least until the driving direction is changed.
obligations.reason: Same alternative ways of satisfying one information obligation as old o052 5.2.2, unchanged.

obligations.text: The long-term deactivation process shall be designed such that deactivation is not possible with less than two deliberate actions.
obligations.reason: Same design requirement as old o052 5.2.2 final sentence.

coverage.source_unit: 5.2.3 heading 'Automatic deactivation'
5.2.3.1 vehicle with automatic deactivation means: following conditions apply as appropriate

obligations.text: When the vehicle is equipped with a means to automatically deactivate the ACPE, for instance in situations such as carrying a bicycle rack or towing a trailer, the conditions of the following sub-paragraphs shall apply as appropriate.
obligations.reason: Same introductory applicability obligation as old o054 5.2.3.1, same scope and wording.

coverage.source_unit: 5.2.3.1.1 – manufacturer shall provide list of automatic deactivation situations and criteria to technical service at type-approval, annexed to test report

obligations.text: Where the vehicle is equipped with a means to automatically deactivate the ACPE, the vehicle manufacturer shall provide to the technical service at the time of type-approval a list of situations and corresponding criteria in which the ACPE is automatically deactivated, and this list shall be annexed to the test report.
obligations.reason: Same scoped obligation as o055 (5.2.3.1.1), identical wording, same parent 5.2.3.1 context and same paragraph number; page shifted only.

coverage.source_unit: 5.2.3.1.2 – ACPE automatically reactivated when deactivation conditions no longer present

obligations.text: Where the vehicle is equipped with a means to automatically deactivate the ACPE, the ACPE shall be automatically reactivated as soon as the conditions that led to the automatic deactivation are no longer present.
obligations.reason: Identical to o056 (5.2.3.1.2) with same parent context and scope.

coverage.source_unit: 5.2.3.1.3 – deactivation warning at least at time of deactivation unless failure warning given per 5.3.3

obligations.text: Where the vehicle is equipped with a means to automatically deactivate the ACPE, a deactivation warning shall be given at least at the time of deactivation, unless a failure warning is given as per paragraph 5.3.3.
obligations.reason: Identical to o057 (5.2.3.1.3) with same parent context and scope.

coverage.source_unit: 5.2.3.1.3.1 first sentence – while an ADS (e.g. ALKS) is in control, ACPE may be suspended or strategies adapted without driver indication if risk mitigation is equal
5.2.3.1.3.1 second sentence – manufacturer shall document and demonstrate suspension/adapted strategies to Approval Authority during safety concept inspection per Annex 3

obligations.text: While an Automated Driving System (e.g. ALKS) is in control of the vehicle, the ACPE may be suspended or its control strategies adapted without indication to the driver, as long as the risks associated with pedal misapplication remain mitigated to the same degree as provided by the ACPE.
obligations.reason: Same permission and condition as o058 (5.2.3.1.3.1), identical wording and parent context.

obligations.text: The vehicle manufacturer shall document and demonstrate to the Approval Authority, during the inspection of the safety concept as part of the assessment to Annex 3, the suspension of the ACPE or the adapted control strategies applied while an Automated Driving System is in control of the vehicle.
obligations.reason: Same documentation/demonstration obligation as second sentence of o058 (5.2.3.1.3.1); continuity of scope with the ADS suspension case.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3 heading – Failure detection / self-check
5.3.1 first sentence – failure warning to driver when ACPE failure prevents meeting requirements
5.3.1 second sentence – warning shall be as specified in 5.4.3

obligations.text: A failure warning shall be given to the driver when there is a failure in the ACPE that prevents the requirements of this Regulation from being met.
obligations.reason: Identical to first sentence of o060 (5.3.1) with same parent 5.3 scope.

obligations.text: The failure warning given to the driver for an ACPE failure that prevents the requirements of this Regulation being met shall be as specified in paragraph 5.4.3.
obligations.reason: Identical to second sentence of o060 (5.3.1); same cross-reference to 5.4.3.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.1.1 whole paragraph: no requirement to provide failure warning signal when ACPE is temporarily unavailable (e.g. inclement weather)

obligations.text: The driver need not be given a failure warning signal indicating that the ACPE is temporarily not available, for example due to inclement weather conditions.
obligations.reason: Same scoped permission/exemption under failure detection 5.3.1 as in o061 (identical wording and parent 5.3.1, page shift only).

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.2 first sentence: no appreciable interval between ACPE self-checks and no delay in illuminating warning signal for electrically detectable failure
5.3.2 second sentence: permission to suppress warning signal if speed >10 km/h at failure detection until speed is below 10 km/h

obligations.text: There shall not be an appreciable time interval between each ACPE self-check, and there shall not be a delay in illuminating the warning signal, in the case of an electrically detectable failure.
obligations.reason: Identical requirement to o062 5.3.2 under same parent 5.3; unchanged.

obligations.text: If the vehicle speed is greater than 10 km/h at the time an electrically detectable failure is detected, the warning signal may be suppressed until the next time the vehicle speed is below 10 km/h.
obligations.reason: Same permission as in o062 5.3.2 with identical scope and value.

coverage.source_unit: 5.3.3 whole paragraph: failure warning for detected non-electrical failure unless deactivation warning given per 5.2.3.1.3

obligations.text: A failure warning shall also be given to the driver in the case of a detected non-electrical failure condition (e.g. sensor blindness or sensor misalignment) unless a deactivation warning is given as per paragraph 5.2.3.1.3.
obligations.reason: Identical to o063 5.3.3 with same parent and scope; unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 5.4 heading 'Warning signals'
5.4.1 heading 'General'
5.4.1.1 first clause: optical warning signals visible even by daylight
5.4.1.1 second clause: satisfactory condition of signals easily verifiable by driver from driver's seat

obligations.text: The optical warning signals shall be visible even by daylight.
obligations.reason: Same requirement as o066 5.4.1.1 under same parent 5.4.1; unchanged.

obligations.text: The satisfactory condition of the optical warning signals shall be easily verifiable by the driver from the driver's seat.
obligations.reason: Same verifiability requirement as o066 5.4.1.1; unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 5.4.1.2 first sentence, alternative 1/2: ACPE optical warning signal activation at engine start/run switch 'on' (run) or manufacturer-designated check position
5.4.1.2 second sentence: exception for warning signals shown in a common space

obligations.text: Each ACPE optical warning signal shall be activated either when the engine start (or run, as relevant) switch is turned to the "on" (run) position or when the switch is in a position between "on" (run) and "start" that is designated by the manufacturer as a check position (initial system power-on).
obligations.reason: Same scoped activation requirement as old 5.4.1.2 (o067), same paragraph number, identical wording, actor and scope under 5.4.1 General.

obligations.text: The requirement that each ACPE optical warning signal be activated at engine start/run switch 'on' (run) or manufacturer-designated check position does not apply to warning signals shown in a common space.
obligations.reason: Same exemption as the second sentence of old 5.4.1.2 (o067), unchanged scope: warning signals shown in a common space.

coverage.source_unit: 5.4.2 para 1 sentence 1: intervention warning given by optical signal
5.4.2 para 1 sentence 2: additional haptic or acoustic signal unless provided by another object detection system
5.4.2 para 2: optical signal may be flashing of failure warning signal (permission)
5.4.2 para 3: manufacturer to provide description of warning indication at type-approval and record in test report
5.4.2 heading

obligations.text: An intervention warning shall be given by an optical signal.
obligations.reason: Same as old 5.4.2 (o068): identical actor, object and scope, same paragraph.

obligations.text: In addition to the optical signal, a haptic or acoustic intervention warning signal shall be provided to the driver, unless such a signal is already being provided by another vehicle system comprising an object detection capability (e.g. parking distance warning).
obligations.reason: Same as old 5.4.2 (o068) additional signal requirement with the same exception.

obligations.text: The optical intervention warning signal may be the flashing of the failure warning signal.
obligations.reason: Same permission as in old 5.4.2 (o068).

obligations.text: The vehicle manufacturer shall provide a description of the warning indication presented to the driver at the time of type-approval, and it shall be recorded in the test report.
obligations.reason: Same documentation obligation as in old 5.4.2 (o068), unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 5.4.3 sentence: failure warning given by constant yellow optical signal
5.4.3 heading

obligations.text: The failure warning shall be given by a constant yellow optical signal.
obligations.reason: Identical to old 5.4.3 (o069), same paragraph, same scope.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5 heading: Provisions for the Periodic Technical Inspection
5.5.1 sentence 1: at PTI, possible to confirm ACPE operational status by visible observation of failure warning signal status
5.5.1 sentence 2: after power-ON and bulb check, failure warning signal remains illuminated if failure present at end of previous cycle unless no longer present
5.5.1 para 2: when failure warning signal in a common space, common space must be observed functional before status check

obligations.text: At a Periodic Technical Inspection, it shall be possible to confirm the correct operational status of the ACPE by a visible observation of the failure warning signal status.
obligations.reason: Same as old 5.5.1 (o071), same paragraph and PTI scope.

obligations.text: Following a power-ON and any bulb check, the failure warning signal shall remain illuminated if any failure was present at the end of the previous engine start (or run, as relevant) cycle, unless this failure is detected to be no longer present.
obligations.reason: Same as old 5.5.1 (o071) failure latching requirement.

obligations.text: Where the failure warning signal is in a common space, the common space must be observed to be functional prior to the failure warning signal status check at the Periodic Technical Inspection.
obligations.reason: Same as old 5.5.1 (o071) second paragraph.

coverage.source_unit: 5.5.2 sentence 1: at type approval, manufacturer's means to protect against simple unauthorised modification of failure warning signal operation confidentially outlined
5.5.2 sentence 2: alternative fulfilment via secondary means of checking ACPE status

obligations.text: At the time of type approval, the means chosen by the manufacturer to protect against simple unauthorised modification of the operation of the failure warning signal shall be confidentially outlined.
obligations.reason: Same as old 5.5.2 (o072), identical scope.

obligations.text: The protection requirement against simple unauthorised modification of the failure warning signal operation is alternatively fulfilled when a secondary means of checking the correct operational status of the ACPE is available.
obligations.reason: Same alternative compliance provision as old 5.5.2 (o072).

coverage.source_unit: 6. Test procedure (heading)
6.1. Test surface and environment conditions (heading)
coverage.exclusion_reason: Heading only; obligations are in sub-paragraphs 6.1.1-6.1.4.

coverage.source_unit: 6.1.1 test on flat, dry, concrete or asphalt road with good adhesion

obligations.text: The test shall be performed on a flat, dry, concrete or asphalt road affording good adhesion.
obligations.reason: Same test-surface requirement as old o075 (6.1.1), same paragraph number, same scope and wording under test surface and environment conditions; no substantive change.

coverage.source_unit: 6.1.2 test surface slope between level and 1 per cent

obligations.text: The test surface shall have a consistent slope between level and 1 per cent.
obligations.reason: Same test-surface slope limit as old o076 (6.1.2), same paragraph and scope; unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 6.1.3 ambient temperature 0°C to 45°C

obligations.text: The ambient temperature during the test shall be between 0°C and 45°C.
obligations.reason: Same ambient temperature condition as old o077 (6.1.3), same paragraph and values; unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 6.1.4 horizontal visibility range allows target to be observed throughout test

obligations.text: The horizontal visibility range shall allow the target to be observed throughout the test.
obligations.reason: Same visibility requirement as old o078 (6.1.4), same paragraph and scope; unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 6.1.5 – tests performed only when no wind liable to affect results

obligations.text: Tests shall be performed when there is no wind liable to affect the results.
obligations.reason: Same paragraph number 6.1.5 under same parent 'Test surface and environment conditions'; identical wording and scope, only page changed.

coverage.source_unit: 6.1.6 first sentence – ambient illumination homogeneous in test area and above 1000 lux
6.1.6 second sentence – ensure testing not performed driving towards/away from sun at low angle

obligations.text: Natural ambient illumination must be homogeneous in the test area and in excess of 1000 lux.
obligations.reason: Matches old 6.1.6 with the same scope under the same parent (test surface and environment conditions); no change.

obligations.text: It should be ensured that testing is not performed whilst driving towards, or away from, the sun at a low angle.
obligations.reason: Matches the second sentence of old 6.1.6 with the same scope; no change.

coverage.source_unit: 6.1.7 – permission for tests under deviating conditions at manufacturer request with Technical Service agreement, performance requirements still to be met

obligations.text: At the request of the manufacturer and with the agreement of the Technical Service, tests may be conducted under deviating test conditions (suboptimal conditions, e.g. on a not dry surface; below the specified minimum ambient temperature), whilst the performance requirements are still to be met.
obligations.reason: Identical to old 6.1.7 with the same parent and scope; no substantive change.

coverage.source_unit: 6.2 Instrumentation – heading only
coverage.exclusion_reason: Heading only; no obligation is imposed.

coverage.source_unit: 6.2.1 – vehicle speed measurement accuracy +/- 0.1 km/h

obligations.text: The speed of the vehicle shall be measured with an accuracy of +/- 0.1 km/h.
obligations.reason: Same as old 6.2.1 with the same measured quantity, accuracy value and instrumentation context; the other candidates 6.2.2/6.2.3 cover different quantities.

coverage.source_unit: 6.2.2 – vehicle position measurement accuracy +/- 0.03 m

obligations.text: The position of the vehicle shall be measured with an accuracy of +/- 0.03 m.
obligations.reason: Same as old 6.2.2 with the same measured quantity and accuracy value in the instrumentation context.

coverage.source_unit: 6.2.3 accelerator control force accuracy +/-1 N (if applicable)

obligations.text: During the test procedure, the accelerator control force (if applicable) shall be measured with an accuracy of +/- 1 N.
obligations.reason: Same paragraph number 6.2.3 under same Instrumentation context; identical actor, object and accuracy value as o085.

coverage.source_unit: 6.2.4 first sentence: accelerator control position accuracy +/-1%
6.2.4 second sentence: alternative, at manufacturer's choice, use vehicle's own position sensor

obligations.text: During the test procedure, the accelerator control position shall be measured with an accuracy of +/- 1%.
obligations.reason: Matches o086 (6.2.4) in same Instrumentation context; same object and accuracy.

obligations.text: At the choice of the manufacturer, the accelerator control position measurement may be taken from the vehicle's own position sensor.
obligations.reason: Same permission as in o086 (6.2.4), same scope and actor.

coverage.source_unit: 6.2.5 recording frequency at least 100 Hz

obligations.text: During the test procedure, measurements shall be recorded at a frequency of at least 100 Hz.
obligations.reason: Identical to o087 (6.2.5) in same Instrumentation context.

coverage.source_unit: 6.3 heading 'Test Vehicle'
6.3.1 (a) if requested by manufacturer, vehicle may be driven max 100 km on mixed urban/rural roads to initialise sensors
6.3.1 (b) if requested by manufacturer, vehicle may undergo brake activations to bed in service brake
6.3.1 final sentence: details of requested pre-test conditioning shall be identified and recorded in type approval documentation

obligations.text: If requested by the vehicle manufacturer, the vehicle can be driven a maximum of 100 km on a mixture of urban and rural roads with other traffic and roadside furniture to initialise the sensor system before the test.
obligations.reason: Same pre-test conditioning permission as o089 (6.3.1(a)), same context.

obligations.text: If requested by the vehicle manufacturer, the vehicle can undergo a sequence of brake activations to ensure the service brake system is bedded in prior to the test.
obligations.reason: Same pre-test conditioning permission as o089 (6.3.1(b)), same context.

obligations.text: Details of the pre-test condition strategy requested by the vehicle manufacturer shall be identified and recorded in the vehicle type approval documentation.
obligations.reason: Same recording obligation as in o089 (6.3.1), same scope.

coverage.source_unit: 6.3.2 first sentence: prior to testing ensure ACPE switched on and ready
6.3.2 second sentence: technical service shall ensure ACPE boundary conditions for target detection are taken into account during test (examples)

obligations.text: Prior to any testing, it shall be ensured that the ACPE is switched on and ready to function.
obligations.reason: Identical to o090 (6.3.2) with same paragraph and Test Vehicle context.

obligations.text: During the conduct of the test, the technical service shall ensure that the boundary conditions of the ACPE, as defined by the manufacturer, with regard to detection of the test target are taken into account (e.g. avoid blocking a sonar system used; ensure a vision system can properly identify the pedestrian test target as a human by making it fully visible to the camera before testing).
obligations.reason: New sentence added to 6.3.2; o090 only contains the first sentence, and no candidate has a boundary-condition requirement for the technical service.

coverage.source_unit: 6.3.3 intro + (a): vehicle tested at minimum mass (running order mass plus max 125 kg additional)
6.3.3 (b) permission: technical service may test at any other mass up to technically permissible maximum laden mass if justified
6.3.3 (b) last sentence: no alteration once test procedure has begun

obligations.text: The vehicle shall be tested at the minimum mass (mass in running order with an additional mass of maximum 125 kg).
obligations.reason: Same scoped test-mass requirement as old 6.3.3(a); identical paragraph number and wording, relocated only in page.

obligations.text: If deemed justified, the technical service may test the vehicle at any other mass up to the technically permissible maximum laden mass as defined by the manufacturer.
obligations.reason: Same permission as old 6.3.3(b), same paragraph and wording.

obligations.text: No alteration to the vehicle test mass shall be made once the test procedure has begun.
obligations.reason: Same sentence as in old 6.3.3(b); unchanged scope.

coverage.source_unit: 6.4 heading 'Test Targets'
6.4.1 target for vehicle detection tests: series production M1 passenger car or soft target per ISO 19206-1:2018 or ISO 19206-3:2021 at manufacturer's choice

obligations.text: The target used for the vehicle detection tests shall be a regular high-volume series production passenger car of Category M1 or alternatively a "soft target" representative of a passenger vehicle in terms of its identification characteristics applicable to the sensor system of the ACPE under test according to either ISO 19206-1:2018 or ISO 19206-3:2021 at the choice of the manufacturer.
obligations.reason: Identical to old 6.4.1 with same paragraph number and scope.

coverage.source_unit: 6.4.2 pedestrian detection test target: child articulated soft target at rest, articulation off, per ISO 19206-2:2018

obligations.text: The targets used for the pedestrian detection tests shall be a child articulated "soft target" in its resting position with the articulation switched off, representative of the human attributes applicable to the sensor system of the ACPE under test according to ISO 19206-2:2018.
obligations.reason: New paragraph; candidate old 6.4.1 covers only vehicle detection targets, no pedestrian target requirement found in old text.

coverage.source_unit: 6.5 heading 'Offset of vehicle and target'
6.5.1 reference point for vehicle location: most rearward centreline point when reversing, most forward point when going forwards

obligations.text: In the offset of vehicle and target test setup, the reference point for the location of the vehicle shall be the most rearward point on the centreline of the vehicle when going rearwards, and the most forward point of the vehicle when going forwards.
obligations.reason: New paragraph; no candidate old clause defines the vehicle reference point (old 6.5 gives offset and distances only, not a reference point).

coverage.source_unit: 6.5.2 lateral offset between vehicle target centreline and vehicle centreline between 0.0 m and distance to extreme outer edge of vehicle

obligations.text: In the test procedure, the lateral offset between the centreline of the vehicle target and the centreline of the vehicle shall be between 0.0 m and the distance to the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.
obligations.reason: Old o094 set a 0.0-0.2 m offset for a generic target; the new clause is a separately scoped offset limit for the vehicle target (0.0 m to the outer edge of the vehicle). It is a different limit and scope, not a relocation of the old one.

coverage.source_unit: 6.5.3 lateral offset between pedestrian obstacle centreline and vehicle centreline not more than 25 per cent of vehicle width

obligations.text: In the test procedure, the lateral offset between the centre line of the pedestrian obstacle and the centre line of the vehicle shall be not more than 25 per cent of the vehicle width.
obligations.reason: No old clause has a pedestrian-target offset limit relative to vehicle width. Candidates o048, o143 and o055 are unrelated.

coverage.source_unit: 6.5.4 orientation of pedestrian target determined by technical service

obligations.text: The orientation of the pedestrian target shall be determined by the technical service.
obligations.reason: No old clause covers pedestrian target orientation. Candidates o078, o020 and o079 address other topics.

coverage.source_unit: 6.5.5 orientation of vehicle target 0° or 180° per ISO 19206-3:2021, chosen by technical service

obligations.text: The orientation of the vehicle target shall be 0° or 180° respectively as defined in ISO 19206-3:2021, as chosen by the technical service.
obligations.reason: No old clause specifies vehicle target orientation or refers to ISO 19206-3. Candidates o020, o017 and o077 are unrelated.

coverage.source_unit: 6.6 test procedures performed forward and rearward, with ACPE interventions triggered at 1.0 m (+0.1 m) and 1.5 m (-0.1 m) from target position per Table 1

obligations.text: The test procedures shall be performed both in a forward and rearward direction and at least with the ACPE interventions triggered at 1.0 m (+0.1 m tolerance) and 1.5 m (-0.1 m tolerance) distance from the target position (as detailed in Table 1).
obligations.reason: Replaces the last paragraph of old o094 (6.5), which required forward and rearward tests at 1.0 m (+0.1) and 1.5 m (-0.1) from the target. The new text drops the 'with and without an expected ACPE intervention' wording and refers to the distance at which the intervention is triggered rather than the vehicle start position.

coverage.source_unit: Table 1 rows: Forward and Rearward at 1.0 m (+0.1) and 1.5 m (-0.1) distance to target / speed measuring point

obligations.text: Test conditions shall be: Forward at 1.0 m distance to target at the point triggering conditions are achieved / to speed measuring point, tolerance +0.1 m; Forward at 1.5 m, tolerance -0.1 m; Rearward at 1.0 m, tolerance +0.1 m; Rearward at 1.5 m, tolerance -0.1 m.
obligations.reason: Replaces old o095 Table 1, which had the same direction/distance/tolerance combinations. The new table removes the lateral offset and target presence columns and redefines the distance as measured at the point triggering conditions are achieved.

coverage.source_unit: 6.6.1 heading: Test procedure for a stationary vehicle
coverage.exclusion_reason: Heading only; no independent obligation (requirements are in 6.6.1.1 and 6.6.1.2).

coverage.source_unit: 6.6.1.1 first sentence: each Table 1 test condition tested with and without target (stationary vehicle)
6.6.1.1 second sentence: for tests without target ACPE deactivated if necessary; may be combined where feasible

obligations.text: For the stationary-vehicle test procedure, each test condition according to Table 1 shall be tested both with and without the presence of the target.
obligations.reason: New scoped requirement under 6.6.1 stationary-vehicle procedure. Old Table 1 had a presence-of-target column and 6.5 required tests with and without ACPE intervention, but no candidate establishes continuity of this specific scoped obligation; candidates o055/o017/o078 are unrelated.

obligations.text: For stationary-vehicle tests without a target, the ACPE shall be deactivated if necessary; such tests may be combined where feasible.
obligations.reason: New provision for no-target tests in the stationary procedure; o055 concerns manufacturer-provided automatic deactivation criteria, a different obligation. Insufficient evidence of equivalence.

coverage.source_unit: 6.6.1.2 (a) position vehicle at distance to target or speed measurement point per Table 1
6.6.1.2 (b) hold stationary and select driving direction
6.6.1.2 (c) accelerate with neutral steering to achieve triggering conditions before 0.5 km/h
6.6.1.2 (d) record speed at collision point or speed measurement point

obligations.text: For each test with a stationary (non-creeping) vehicle, position the vehicle at the distance to the relevant target or speed measurement point defined in Table 1.
obligations.reason: Replaces step (a) of the procedure in old Table 1 (o095), which was the single procedure; now scoped to stationary vehicle with 'relevant target' wording.

obligations.text: For each test with a stationary (non-creeping) vehicle, hold the vehicle stationary and select the corresponding driving direction.
obligations.reason: Same step (b) relocated from the procedure under old Table 1 (o095) to 6.6.1.2 for the stationary vehicle test, unchanged in substance.

obligations.text: For each test with a stationary (non-creeping) vehicle, accelerate the vehicle by operating the accelerator control while maintaining steering control in the neutral position, so as to achieve the relevant triggering conditions (paragraph 5.1.2) before the vehicle reaches a speed of 0.5 km/h.
obligations.reason: Relocated step (c) of the old Table 1 procedure (o095), the stationary-start accelerate step; wording unchanged.

obligations.text: For each test with a stationary (non-creeping) vehicle, record the speed at the collision point (if applicable) or the speed at the respective speed measurement point.
obligations.reason: Relocated step (d) of the old Table 1 procedure (o095); same recording action and scope.

coverage.source_unit: 6.6.2 heading: Test procedure for a creeping vehicle
6.6.2.1 first sentence: each Table 1 condition tested once with starting point and accelerator profile selected at Technical Service discretion
6.6.2.1 second sentence with (a): trigger as close as practical to max creeping speed forward, at or below it, avoiding AEBS warning/intervention preventing ACPE intervention
6.6.2.1 (b): trigger as close as practical to 4 km/h rearward, at or below it, avoiding AEBS interference

obligations.text: For the creeping-vehicle procedure, each test condition according to Table 1 shall be tested once, with a starting point and accelerator control application profile selected at the discretion of the Technical Service.
obligations.reason: New creeping-vehicle test; no old clause covers creeping tests (o094/o039 address different scope).

obligations.text: In forward creeping tests, the starting point and accelerator control application profile shall be selected such that the triggering condition (paragraph 5.1.2) is achieved as close as reasonably practical to the maximum creeping speed, while remaining at or below that speed and avoiding any AEBS warning or intervention that results in an ACPE intervention not occurring.
obligations.reason: New speed-targeting condition for forward creeping tests; no equivalent in candidates.

obligations.text: In rearward creeping tests, the starting point and accelerator control application profile shall be selected such that the triggering condition (paragraph 5.1.2) is achieved as close as reasonably practical to 4 km/h, while remaining at or below that speed and avoiding any AEBS warning or intervention that results in an ACPE intervention not occurring.
obligations.reason: New speed-targeting condition for rearward creeping tests; no equivalent in candidates.

coverage.source_unit: 6.6.2.2 (a) position at selected starting point per 6.6.2.1
6.6.2.2 (b) hold stationary and select driving direction
6.6.2.2 (c) release braking system so vehicle creeps
6.6.2.2 (d) operate accelerator to achieve triggering conditions at distance to target per Table 1
6.6.2.2 (e) if collision not prevented manufacturer demonstrates compliance with 5.1.6.2

obligations.text: For each creeping-vehicle test, position the vehicle at the starting point selected per paragraph 6.6.2.1.
obligations.reason: New creeping procedure step; old Table 1 procedure positioned vehicle at the Table 1 distance, a different step for stationary starts.

obligations.text: For each creeping-vehicle test, hold the vehicle stationary and select the corresponding driving direction.
obligations.reason: Repeats an action from the old stationary procedure (o095 step b) but under a separately introduced creeping procedure; scoped as new.

obligations.text: For each creeping-vehicle test, release the braking system so that the vehicle starts creeping.
obligations.reason: New creeping-specific step with no old equivalent.

obligations.text: For each creeping-vehicle test, operate the accelerator control to achieve the relevant triggering conditions (paragraph 5.1.2) at the point the vehicle has reached the distance to target according to Table 1.
obligations.reason: New creeping-specific triggering step, differing from the old stationary accelerate-before-0.5 km/h step.

obligations.text: In a creeping-vehicle test where a collision is not prevented, the manufacturer shall demonstrate to the satisfaction of the technical service that the intervention complies with the requirements of paragraph 5.1.6.2.
obligations.reason: New manufacturer demonstration obligation for creeping tests referencing 5.1.6.2; old 5.1.6 is a performance limit, not this demonstration duty.

coverage.source_unit: 6.7 permission: Technical Service may additionally test in any test condition within conditions of paragraph 5.1.5 if justified
6.7 permission: Technical Service may additionally test alternative accelerator control application profiles if justified

obligations.text: If deemed justified, the Technical Service may additionally test in any test condition within the conditions specified in paragraph 5.1.5.
obligations.reason: Candidate o096 (6.6) permits testing within conditions of paragraph 5.1 during tests of 6.5; the new clause refers to a different scope (5.1.5) and is additional to the prescribed tests, so equivalence of the same scoped obligation is not established.

obligations.text: If deemed justified, the Technical Service may additionally test alternative accelerator control application profiles.
obligations.reason: No candidate old clause permits testing alternative accelerator control application profiles.

coverage.source_unit: 7 heading: Modification of vehicle type and extension of approval
7.1 first sentence: every modification of vehicle type shall be notified to the approving Type Approval Authority
7.1 lead-in: Type Approval Authority may either (7.1.1/7.1.2) - handled in sub-clauses
coverage.exclusion_reason: Introductory lead-in to options detailed in 7.1.1 and 7.1.2, which are covered in their own clauses.

obligations.text: Every modification of the vehicle type as defined in paragraph 2.2 shall be notified to the Type Approval Authority which approved the vehicle type.
obligations.reason: Identical to old clause o098 (7.1), same actor, action and scope; unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 7.1.1 option: Type Approval Authority may consider modifications to have no adverse effect and grant an extension of approval

obligations.text: The Type Approval Authority may consider that the modifications made do not have an adverse effect on the conditions of the granting of the approval and grant an extension of approval.
obligations.reason: Identical to old clause o099 (7.1.1) under the same parent 7.1; unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 7.1.2 option: modifications affect approval conditions and require further tests or additional checks before granting an extension

obligations.text: The Type Approval Authority may consider that the modifications made affect the conditions of the granting of the approval and require further tests or additional checks before granting an extension of approval.
obligations.reason: Identical to old clause o100 (7.1.2) under the same parent 7.1; unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 7.2 confirmation or refusal of approval, specifying alterations, shall be communicated per 4.3 to Contracting Parties

obligations.text: Confirmation or refusal of approval, specifying the alterations, shall be communicated by the procedure specified in paragraph 4.3 to the Contracting Parties to the Agreement which apply this Regulation.
obligations.reason: Identical to old clause o101 (7.2) with same actor, procedure and scope; unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 7.3 first sentence: Type Approval Authority shall inform other Contracting Parties of the extension via Annex 1 communication form
7.3 second sentence: assign a serial number (extension number) to each extension

obligations.text: The Type Approval Authority shall inform the other Contracting Parties of an extension of approval by means of the communication form in Annex 1 to this Regulation.
obligations.reason: Same actor, action and scope as old 7.3 (o102) under the same parent paragraph 7; unchanged wording, only page shift.

obligations.text: The Type Approval Authority shall assign a serial number, known as the extension number, to each extension.
obligations.reason: Same obligation as old 7.3 (o102) second sentence, same parent paragraph 7; unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 8 heading: Conformity of production
8.1: CoP procedures shall comply with 1958 Agreement Schedule 1 (E/ECE/TRANS/505/Rev.3) and meet following requirements

obligations.text: Procedures concerning conformity of production shall comply with those set out in the 1958 Agreement, Schedule 1 (E/ECE/TRANS/505/Rev.3) and meet the requirements of paragraphs 8.2 and 8.3.
obligations.reason: Identical to old 8.1 (o104) under the same parent paragraph 8; no change in scope.

coverage.source_unit: 8.2: vehicle shall be manufactured to conform to approved type by meeting requirements of paragraph 5

obligations.text: A vehicle approved pursuant to this Regulation shall be manufactured so as to conform to the approved type by meeting the requirements of paragraph 5.
obligations.reason: Identical to old 8.2 (o105) under the same parent paragraph 8; unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 8.3 first sentence: Type Approval Authority may at any time verify conformity of control methods for each production unit
8.3 second sentence: normal inspection frequency once every two years

obligations.text: The Type Approval Authority which has granted approval may at any time verify the conformity of control methods applicable to each production unit.
obligations.reason: Same permission as old 8.3 (o106) under CoP paragraph 8; unchanged.

obligations.text: The normal frequency of conformity-of-production inspections by the Type Approval Authority shall be once every two years.
obligations.reason: Same frequency requirement as old 8.3 (o106) second sentence; unchanged.

coverage.source_unit: 9 heading: Penalties for non-conformity of production
9.1 – approval may be withdrawn if paragraph 8 requirements not complied with (permission)

obligations.text: The approval granted in respect of a vehicle type pursuant to this Regulation may be withdrawn if the requirements laid down in paragraph 8 (conformity of production) are not complied with.
obligations.reason: Same scoped permission as old 9.1 (o108) under identical parent 'Penalties for non-conformity of production'; wording and scope are unchanged, only the page differs.

coverage.source_unit: 9.2 – Contracting Party withdrawing an approval shall forthwith notify other Contracting Parties using Annex 1 communication form

obligations.text: If a Contracting Party withdraws an approval it had previously granted, it shall forthwith notify the other Contracting Parties applying this Regulation by sending them a communication form conforming to the model in Annex 1 to this Regulation.
obligations.reason: Same actor, action and trigger as old 9.2 (o109) under same parent; unchanged text.

coverage.source_unit: 10 – approval holder who completely ceases manufacture shall inform the Type Approval Authority
10 – Type Approval Authority shall forthwith inform other Contracting Parties via Annex 1 communication form

obligations.text: If the holder of the approval completely ceases to manufacture a type of vehicle approved in accordance with this Regulation, he shall inform the Type Approval Authority which granted the approval.
obligations.reason: Same manufacturer obligation as old clause 10 (o110); text identical.
